page: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the ARM64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 model running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration is supported by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a bundled 1875 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results position the i4g.2xlarge in the average tier for multi-core compute and database operations. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 12132.09 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5360.0. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 472.81 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 116.33 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database performance is solid, with Redis SET operations handling 9.8 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring 5224.61. However, single-core performance is weaker, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0 and a poor bzip3 single-threaded decompression rate of 7.19 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds are also limited, with a 7B model generating 6.74 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i4g.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for storage-heavy workloads by bundling a substantial 1875 GB NVMe SSD directly with ARM-based compute resources. This design avoids the overhead of external network-attached storage. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and strong local storage performance, this instance is highly suited for database deployments, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and moderate-scale data processing tasks that benefit from local scratch space and ARM power efficiency.
